**Genesis vs. NES (Nintendo Entertainment System – the 3‑letter abbreviation)**  

| Feature | Sega Genesis (Mega Drive) | NES |
|---------|---------------------------|-----|
| **CPU** | Motorola 68000, 7.67 MHz (16‑bit) | Ricoh 5A22, 1.79 MHz (8‑bit) |
| **Main RAM** | 64 KB | 2 KB |
| **Video RAM** | 64 KB | 256 B |
| **Sprite limit** | 80 sprites per scan‑line | 20 sprites per scan‑line |
| **Color palette** | 512‑colour set (64 on‑screen) | 54‑colour set (25 on‑screen) |
| **Sound** | Yamaha YM2612 FM (6 channels) + TI SN76489 PSG (3 channels) + PCM buffer → ~12 channels | 2 tone + 1 noise + 1 sample channels → 3 channels |
| **Expansion ports** | Z80 co‑processor + extra‑RAM & peripheral slots | None (cart‑only) |

**Why the Genesis was a step ahead**

| Advantage | What it meant for games |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Faster CPU & more memory | Faster frame rates, larger levels, complex AI |
| Greater sprite capacity | Busiest action scenes, smoother animation |
| Richer color palette | Brighter, more detailed graphics |
| Advanced audio | Better music and realistic sound‑effects |
| Expansion slots | Developers could add sound chips, more RAM, new controllers, etc. |

All of these hardware improvements gave the Genesis an edge in delivering deeper, more realistic sports titles—exactly why Sony‑constituent “NFL ’95” (and other NFL‑licensed games) were far more advanced than what the NES could produce.

**Game that showcases this advantage**

- **Title:** *NFL ’95* (1994) – the first official NFL‑licensed game on the Sega Genesis.  
- **Why it matters:** It used the Genesis’ 16‑bit 7.67 MHz CPU, top‑line sprite handling, 12‑channel FM/PCM sound, and large memory to render full‑season play, real‑time passing, dynamic camera zoom, instant replays, and a 1,500‑player roster—all features that the NES simply couldn’t support with its 8‑bit, 1.79 MHz hardware.

*The Los Angeles Rams are a member of the NFL, so the “football league that the Rams represent” is indeed the NFL, and “NFL ’95” is the Genesis title named after that league.*
